# `comply-no-color-flag`

--no-color wins over FORCE_COLOR, so the CI-facing output carries no escape sequences even on a colour-capable runner.

## What runs

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Command** | `hermex comply --no-color` |
| **Working directory** | `fixtures/` |
| **Config** | [`fixtures/hermex.config.ts`](../hermex.config.ts) |
| **Fixture** | [`fixtures`](..) — [overview](../README.md) |
| **Asserted exit code** | `1` |
| **Environment** | `NO_COLOR` unset, `FORCE_COLOR=3` |
| **Colour** | captured raw, so escape sequences are part of the recorded output |

## Recorded output

The committed baseline is [`tests/__output_baselines__/comply-no-color-flag/`](../../tests/__output_baselines__/comply-no-color-flag), which holds this case's stdout, stderr, exit code and any file it wrote. A change to hermex's output shows up as a diff there, once a reviewer applies `baseline:approved` and the bot regenerates it — see `.github/workflows/baseline-approve.yaml`.
